<reason>Side A won by grounding the case in the robust Portugal evidence, effectively rebutting Oregon as an underfunded outlier during a fentanyl supply shock, and exposing a logical contradiction in Side B's agency argument via pressure questions. Side A maintained coherent causal mechanisms addressing both overdose deaths (reduced fear of seeking help, earlier intervention) and downstream crime (avoiding criminal records that block housing/employment), while Side B relied on contested premises about the efficacy of coercion and enforcement paralysis.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>Side A's Pressure Questions exposed Side B's contradiction: if addiction destroys rational agency making voluntary treatment futile, then threatening incarceration cannot restore that agency through "leverage"; Side B's subsequent pivot to "physical interruption" in Rebuttal 2 failed to fully resolve this logical tension, leaving its core mechanism unstable.</best_rebuttal>
